text.p: - Slovenia's parliament on Wednesday refused all suggested changes to the current referendum procedures.
- Slovenian unions protested against an announcement by the Chamber of Economy which said that current workers' benefits were too high for many Slovenian companies.
- Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek presented Slovenia's arguments for candidacy for the United Nations' Security Council to the U.N. assembly on Wednesday.
- The damaged border tunnel Ljubelj between Slovenia and Austria will be opened by October 20, Slovenia's Office for State Roads said.
- The parliament decided to prohibit the production and import of concrete products that include asbestos from December 20.
- The Association of Employers said many Slovenian companies were facing financial problems because of high taxes, high interest rates and an expensive workforce.
- A five-day fair, Narava-zdravje, introducing healthy food, cosmetics and drug products opened in Ljubljana on Wednesday.
- Olimpija Ljubljana beat German Leverkusen Bayer in a Euroleague basketball match on Wednesday.
